memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph stayed in Egypt, along with all his father's family. He lived a hundred and ten years and saw the third generation of Ephraim's children. Also the children of Makir son of Manasseh were placed at birth on Joseph's knees." — Gen 50:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph lives to a hundred and ten and sees his great-great-grandchildren. Babies are placed on his knees — the old man who was once thrown in a pit, holding the next generation.

There is enormous gentleness in that picture. God gave Joseph decades of ordinary, peaceful family life after the drama was over. The dreams, the famine, the reconciliation — all behind him. What remains is grandchildren on his knees.

We tend to think of a well-lived life in terms of its dramatic moments. Joseph's story is mostly remembered for the pit, the prison and the palace. But most of his years were quiet ones, and Scripture records them without apology.

If your life feels undramatic — work, family, church, ordinary faithfulness — you are not failing. You may be living the part of the story God most wanted to give you. Paul told the Thessalonians to make it their ambition to lead a quiet life (1 Thess 4:11), which is a strange sort of ambition, and a good one.

Faithfulness across ordinary decades is its own kind of testimony. Children on your knees is not a small thing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you undervalue the ordinary seasons of your life?
2. What does faithfulness look like for you in this particular season?
3. Who is watching your ordinary life more closely than you realise?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the quiet seasons as well as the dramatic ones. Help me be faithful in the ordinary years and not despise them. Amen.
